reason: User clause: no change from IT and ITES use without consent, to protect the Building's approvals. Restricts use of these premises only.
Loss of the deposit on early exit. Whether that is a penalty is a s.74 question.

The Lessor will not let space in the Building for software development during the Exclusivity Term (the first 5 years of the term, cl. 1.1B). A restriction on how the Lessor deals with its own property, in-term only.
The Lessor's damage determination binds only 'unless and until it is set aside or varied in arbitration under clause 18(b)'. The forum is preserved (as PO-42).
Interest at 2% a month (24% a year) on late rent. It does not limit recourse to courts. Whether the rate is penal is a s.74 question.
The Cooling-off Period (cl. 4.1A) is the year after the Lease Period ends, so this is a post-lease restraint (2 km, software and ITES, including through affiliates). No goodwill sold. Void.
On determination of the lease, the Lessee must stop BPO business in the taluk and not resume it for 4 years. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.
Three years after the amount falls due, the same as the Limitation Act period (Arts. 52, 55, 113). Not shorter, so not void.
Suits for possession and rent arrears go to the Bangalore courts, where the property is (s.16 CPC). Those courts have jurisdiction anyway. Valid.

This is not a covenant about letting. For 2 years after the deed, the Lessor (SIPCOT) may not itself carry on, or be interested in, a software business from the Building or its adjoining property. A post-lease restraint on the Lessor's own trade, with no goodwill sold. Void. (Contrast the 'will not let to competitors' covenants, which go to refer only when they run past the term.)

Claims for maintenance adjustments 'shall stand extinguished' unless made by the Reconciliation Date (30 days after the quarter, cl. 1B). The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period. Section 28 protects both sides. Void.
Mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential loss. Limits recovery, not access to court (as PO-55).
Service-charge disputes 'shall be referred' to a sole arbitrator under the 1996 Act, with a final award. A binding arbitration agreement, saved by Exception 1.

The Lessor's own determination of the fit-out-ready date is final and 'shall not be questioned ... in any forum whatsoever'. One party decides and every forum, including cl. 18 arbitration, is shut out. Void.

The Lessee may raise no dispute 'by suit, arbitration or otherwise' about parking allocation, and the Lessor's allocation is final. One party decides and no forum is left for that class of claims, overriding cl. 18(d). Void to that extent.
An ordinary rent payment date. Says nothing about claims or courts.
Repayment of the rent-free period on termination within the lock-in. A clawback of a concession: whether it is a penalty is a s.74 question.

An independent structural engineer, nominated by the President of the Institution of Engineers, whose determination of a technical fact binds both sides. An agreed way of fixing a fact; courts are not expressly excluded, and cl. 16 arbitration remains. Refer, per the BP-7 approach.

A right of first offer: while the lease subsists, the Lessor will not allot campus space to a competing business without offering it to the Lessee first. A restriction on how the Lessor deals with its own property, in-term only.
The Long-Stop Period (cl. 1B) is 3 years 6 months from the end of the lease, longer than the 3-year period for damages (Art. 55). It does not restrict the right to sue. Not void.

The Lessor sold the goodwill of the Acquired Business (cl. 4.1B) to the Lessee, and restrains itself within the municipal limits of Chennai (a specified local limit) for as long as the buyer or its assigns carry on a like business at the Building. All three conditions of Exception 1 are met, and whether the limits are reasonable is for the court. Refer.
Claims for repair costs are 'forfeited' unless presented within 3 months of the repairs. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period. Void.

Exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Chennai, but the land is at Nanakramguda, Hyderabad, both parties have their registered offices in Hyderabad, and the deed was executed there. Nothing connects Chennai, and parties cannot confer jurisdiction (A.B.C. Laminart). An exclusive choice of a court without jurisdiction ousts the competent ones. Void. It also conflicts with the deed's own Hyderabad clause (after cl. 6.9) and the cl. 6.8 arbitration.

Giving up an injunction alone would be a remedies point. But the Lessee also may not 'claim damages in any forum' for the works, and may not approach 'any court, tribunal or arbitrator'. That leaves no forum for that class of claims. Void to that extent.
At least 30 days' notice before starting arbitration. A minimum notice, not a deadline: nothing is lost, the claim just waits (as PO-40).
Readings stand for billing unless a joint reading is asked for within 7 days, but the Lessee expressly keeps the right to a refund of anything wrongly charged. No right is lost.
User clause during the Lease Period: no hazardous materials and no manufacturing. Restricts use of these premises only.
Post-lease restraint (12 months, anywhere in Coimbatore). No goodwill sold. Void.

The Lessor's own computation of escalated rent is conclusive, and the dispute may not go to arbitration under cl. 39 nor be the subject of 'any suit or other proceeding'. One party decides and every forum is shut out. Void to that extent.

'Finally settled by arbitration' under the ICA Rules (cl. 1C), with the award enforceable in any competent court. A binding arbitration agreement, saved by Exception 1. (It sits alongside cl. 12A, which names a different procedure; that inconsistency is for the arbitral tribunal or court, not s.28.)
A damages action must be commenced within 18 months of the breach or be 'barred', against 3 years under Art. 55. Shortens the time to sue. Void.

Goodwill is sold under the Business Transfer (cl. 1.1B), but the restraint is 'anywhere in India' and for a fixed 5 years, not for as long as the buyer carries on the business. Two conditions of Exception 1 are missing. Void.
For breach of quiet enjoyment the Lessee gets only an abatement of rent. That limits the relief, not the forum; the Lessee can still arbitrate or sue for the abatement. A remedies question, not s.28.

A dispute not referred by the Reference Deadline (4 months, cl. 1.1C) is 'deemed to be finally settled' and cannot be raised 'in any forum'. The right is extinguished on the expiry of a period, against the 3-year period (s.43 of the 1996 Act). Void.
The Lessor's liability to reimburse stamp duty 'shall cease absolutely' unless claimed within a month of renewal. A discharge from liability on the expiry of a period. Void.
For 12 months after the Lease ends, no mobile security software business in the zone or estate, binding the Lessee and its group. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void.

During the Post-Lease Period (6 months after the lease, cl. 1A), no networking office in the same complex, binding the Lessee and anyone claiming through it. A post-lease restraint with no goodwill sold. Void however short.

The Lessor's own Final Measurement Certificate (cl. 1C) becomes conclusive, and the Lessee 'shall not be entitled to dispute' the area, unless it objects within 21 days. A deemed-acceptance clause that takes away the right on the expiry of a period (as PO-14, PO-24 and PO-66). Void.

The Lessor's Architect is appointed by the Lessor (cl. 1B), and his determination may not be 'called in question before any court, arbitral tribunal or authority'. A party's nominee with every forum expressly excluded, so not the BP-7 refer case. Void.
The Suit Period (cl. 1D) is 2 years from the breach, against 3 years under Art. 55 (and 12 years for possession under Art. 67). Shortens the time to sue. Void.

The Lease Duration (cl. 1B) is the term only, so this is in-term, but it bars the business at any other location within 10 km. That is business elsewhere, and the landlord's interest is not apparent from the deed (as PO-11, PO-39). Refer.
A notice step (report a leak within 48 hours). No consequence for claims or courts.

On its own this is void: 'may be referred ... if they can agree on one' is not an arbitration agreement (Jagdish Chander), and the civil courts are barred 'in no event'. But cl. 5A of this deed sends 'any dispute' to arbitration with 'shall', so a forum is left if 5A governs. The two clauses conflict on how the arbitrator is chosen, and 22A would also keep the courts out of their role under the 1996 Act (ss. 9, 11 and 34). They need reading together, as in PO-59. Refer; worth discussing in Session 2.

On its own this is void: 'may be referred' is not an arbitration agreement (Jagdish Chander), and the courts are excluded, so it is an absolute bar. But this deed also has cls. 5A and 12A, both binding agreements to arbitrate 'any dispute'. Read with them, a forum remains and the court exclusion is the ordinary effect of arbitration, though it would still keep the courts out of their role under the 1996 Act. Needs the clauses read together (as PO-59). Refer; worth discussing.

The Radius Restriction (cl. 1C) applies only while the Lessee holds the lease, but it restrains trade from any other shop within 1 km. That is business elsewhere. The turnover rent is the commercial justification a court would weigh, and that depends on context the text does not settle. Refer.
